intent: I took the Integrator's advice on the oscillation trigger and narrowed the sensor row from plus or minus 0.04 m to plus or minus 0.02 m at 10 mm spacing. I also moved the row from y = 0.06 to y = 0.04 to cut the sensing lag. I kept the 12 mm footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, body and mass unchanged so the effect of the sensor layout can be read directly. Expected result: lower steering oscillation on the slalom and s-bend, fewer off-track endings, and higher progress than iteration 0. I am considering a further forward offset (about 0.02 m) or a 16 mm footprint for later, but I am not committing to either yet.
learning: Off-track endings at max error of about 0.06 m are the binding failure in every track, so the off-track limit can only be respected by keeping the robot closer to the line. Open hypotheses: (1) the single line-loss event per run happens at start-up or at the first sharp bend, which a narrower row might still produce if the sensors lose the line at larger offsets; (2) a row closer to the axle reduces oscillation; (3) a 12 mm footprint gives a cleaner signal than 16 mm on 25 mm tape. Please report the progress at which the first line loss occurs on each track, because that will show whether the loss is on a bend or at start-up.
rationale: The race evidence is clear but does not yet isolate a cause. All 60 trials on the three development tracks ended off track, with no finishes. Progress stopped at 0.11 to 0.15, and each run recorded one line-loss event. Max error reached about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit for this body (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06). So the robot loses the line early and drifts out rather than stalling. Steering oscillation is highest on the s-bend (0.143) and slalom (0.153), and lowest on the oval (0.072), which matches the Integrator's second pattern: oscillation tied to the sharper track features. The Integrator's advice was conditional. Their first trigger (line loss on bends) is present in the sense that the single loss happens on every track, but it is not clearly tied to bends. Their second trigger (oscillation on the slalom) is present. Following their advice, I am narrowing the row to plus or minus 0.02 m with 12 mm footprints. I am also moving the row closer to the axle, from y = 0.06 to y = 0.04. The reason is that the current sensors sit 6 cm ahead of the wheels, so the controller reacts to the line about 0.06 m before the wheels respond, and that lag can amplify oscillation. With the row at plus or minus 0.02 m, any sensor still sees the tape until the robot is offset by about 0.038 m, which is before the 0.06 m off-track limit. The current wide row covers offsets up to about 0.058 m, so it gives little warning before the run ends. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit: the limit only rises above 0.06 m at body widths over 0.19 m, which is outside the allowed range. Expected result: lower steering oscillation on the slalom and s-bend, fewer off-track endings, and a higher progress. Completion is not yet expected, because the controller has not been changed.
